prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1109; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: The claimant reported a rear-end collision at a low-speed intersection and said their neck and upper back hurt immediately afterward. The reported injury fits the kind and force of this impact well, and the claimant is not represented by an attorney.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy record and confirmed the driver is named on the policy and was covered at the time of loss. Nothing suggests the damage occurred before the coverage period started.

Entry 3: Spoke with the claimant by phone to take a recorded statement. The account of how the collision happened was consistent with what was first reported.

Entry 4: Received photos from the claimant showing rear bumper and trunk damage. The photos confirm some details of the impact, and the vehicle damage matches the described collision.

Entry 5: Requested the police report, which confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the scene. Attempted to locate independent witnesses, but none have come forward and no third-party accounts are available.

Entry 6: Ran a prior claims and medical history search. No earlier injury to the neck or upper back has been found, and no earlier damage to the vehicle is on record.

Entry 7: Authorized an independent vehicle inspection. The inspector's estimate lines up with the damage pattern shown in the photos and with the reported point of impact.

Entry 8: Called the claimant for a follow-up. They repeated the same account of the collision that was given in the first report and the recorded statement, with no changes in the sequence of events.

Entry 9: Treatment has continued for somewhat longer than is typical for this type of injury. Requested treatment records and itemized bills from the provider to review the care plan against standard guidelines.

Entry 10: Reviewed the file with the claims supervisor. Coverage is confirmed, the injury and vehicle damage are consistent with the collision, and the claim will proceed to evaluation of the medical records and the length of treatment.
